source_review.notes: Reviewed all ten references. Coherence-aware waiting and scalable synchronization were checked against Anderson and Mellor-Crummey/Scott; elimination and combining against Hendler-Shavit-Yerushalmi and Hendler et al.; NUMA/synchronization measurement against Dice et al. and David et al.; durable algorithm context against Herlihy-Shavit; and current target/scheduler guidance against Intel, Arm, and Linux documentation. Six sources resolved directly and four ACM publisher pages denied automated retrieval; those pages support bibliographic and scoped result attribution only, not inaccessible quotations or details.

evidence: Definitions and Notation consistently defines attempts A, commits C, failures F, retry amplification RA, conflict count k_i, capped window W_i, delay D_i, contenders N, and offered/sustainable rates lambda/mu.
The chapter separates abstract commitment, stuttering delay, retry policy, alternate linearization paths, fairness, logical progress, scheduler blocking, overload, and measurement.
notation_and_syntax.notes: Checked C>0 domain, one-successful-attempt assumption, saturating/capped arithmetic, delay interval, and capacity inequality terminology.

evidence: For eight attempts and one commit, recomputed RA=8 and F=7.

numerical_recomputation.notes: The slot choices are stipulated deterministic evidence, not a stochastic expectation or hardware benchmark.

evidence: Wait/yield/park steps map to abstract stuttering and must be followed by full witness refresh; only the original or separately proved alternate commitment changes abstract state.
When offered rate lambda exceeds sustainable mu, unbounded demand cannot be stabilized by backoff alone; admission, bounded queueing, rejection, reduced demand, or increased capacity is required.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: Randomized collision reduction is not used as deterministic fairness, termination, or latency proof.

evidence: Reviewed zero/one/many contenders, synchronized retries, low/moderate/saturation/overload, cap and overflow, correlated seeds, starvation, oversubscription, SMT, NUMA, skew, and thermal/scheduler effects.

Reviewed stale protection, repeated side effects, lost wakeups, token leaks, elimination timeout/mismatch/ABA, stalled combiner, batch cancellation, shard migration/global order, priority inversion, close/shutdown, and high-stakes deadlines.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Boundary analysis spans retry correctness, probability, scheduler, topology, alternate mechanisms, ownership, overload, measurement, lifecycle, and safety.

evidence: Every operation has one effect/result; failures and delays stutter; all derived state refreshes; no wait holds a competitor-needed resource; backoff arithmetic and tokens remain bounded/owned.
Elimination pairs complementary calls once, combiner/helper requests publish results once, shards preserve declared semantics, and cancellation/close are ordered against commitment.
invariant_checking.notes: Checked invariants across load, conflict, release protection, delay, refresh, retry, admit, park/wake, eliminate, combine, help, batch, shard/migrate, cancel, close, drain, and destroy.

evidence: The safety proof retains the original linearization point for pure delay and requires each alternate path to refine one legal abstract transition without duplication.

The progress review qualifies pure retry reasoning with eventual attempt assumptions and explicitly removes unqualified lock-free claims when parking, admission queues, combiner locks, allocation, or scheduler dependencies enter.
proof_review.notes: This is internal proof review of policies and obligations, not source refinement, probabilistic tail proof, real-time analysis, or production performance certification.

evidence: Linearizability, lock-free kernel progress, end-to-end blocking, starvation/fairness, overload stability, tail latency, energy, and scalability remain distinct claims.
Backoff, elimination, combining, helping, sharding, and mutex/admission alternatives state their changed assumptions and proof surfaces.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: Analytical model, deterministic illustration, empirical benchmark, target documentation, operational policy, and named human safety review remain separate.

evidence: python3 tools/verify_snippets.py CONPAR-059 passed the deterministic slot-collision model with recorded Python version, exact stdout, empty stderr, and zero exit code.

The chapter requires controlled-seed tests, real workload/topology matrices, schedule/weak-memory/sanitizer checks, target atomic inspection, overload/cancellation/shutdown faults, hardware/runtime metrics, and a simpler baseline.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: The sequential pair count proves no randomness quality, concurrency, cache behavior, fairness, progress, latency, energy, throughput, overload safety, or deployment result.

conceptual_review.notes: Reviewed hot-path accounting, retry safety, storms, backoff, spin/yield/park, admission, elimination, combining/delegation, sharding, helping/priority, measurement, lifecycle/telemetry, and alternatives.

practitioner_review.notes: Reviewed instrumentation without hot counters, overflow-safe windows, injectable jitter, protection release before delay, lost-wakeup-safe parking, overload results, exact tokens/arena/request ownership, target/topology qualification, configuration rollout, fallback, and clean drain.

pedagogical_review.notes: The review sheet foregrounds useful work versus retries; exposition moves from correctness to policy and structural alternatives; the collision model is reproducible; ten examples are distinct; and five exercises progress from metrics to medical-telemetry transfer with complete matching answers.

limitations: Internal authoring, source, mathematical, snippet, conceptual, practitioner, and pedagogical evidence only; no external concurrency-theory, probability, performance, C++/Java/Rust, compiler, architecture, scheduler, NUMA, real-time, automotive, medical, regulatory, operational, cybersecurity, or safety review is claimed. The chapter and model establish neither source correctness nor linearizability, lock-free progress, fairness, randomness quality, overload stability, target performance, latency bounds, resource boundedness, or deployment safety.
